subject: Change fonts of facet, use subscript

messages.author: 09769225ad45054d
messages.subject: Change fonts of facet, use subscript
parts:
Hello,

I wish to change the text of strip. As an example I wish Death instead of death, CVD instead of cvd, and PM10 (PM and subscript 10)  instead of pm10. I could obtain  some, but not all,  of the desired results by changing the names of columns.

How could I obtain these results? Data are found below.



library(dlnm)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

df <- chicagoNMMAPS

df1<-df[c(1,7:8,13)]

dmelt = melt(df1, id.vars = 'date')
ggplot(dmelt, aes(x = date, y = value)) + 
  theme_bw() +
    geom_line() + 
    facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = 'free_y', ncol = 1)+ 
  theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size=14,face="bold",angle = 30),
          strip.background = element_rect(colour="blue", fill="#CCCCFF")) + 
    theme(axis.title=element_text(size="12") ,axis.text=element_text(size=14))



Thanks

messages.author: f20966e9bc9cf5c7
messages.subject: Re: Change fonts of facet, use subscript
parts:
Hi Nici,

You're on the right track except for wishing death with the a capital D ;)!

See: http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Facets_%28ggplot2%29/

dmelt$variable = revalue(dmelt$variable, death="Death", PM10="PM[10]")

Then check out
?label_parser

Cheers,
Brian
